text:
Maria K: Heads-up: we've had several postmortem action items slip >30d. I'd like to prototype a lightweight recurring follow-up to keep owners honest and to detect recurring incident classes. Proposal below.

Jamal R: Whats the shape of the follow-up? Weekly? Owners only?

Maria K: Weekly 15m sync focused strictly on open remediation items: owner, ETA, blocker, verifier. Keep notes to 1-3 bullets per item. Rotation: the IC on duty facilitates the meeting that week.

Alex T: 👍 for weekly + a monthly trends review. Weekly stays tactical; monthly we surface recurring fixes and SLO impact.

Sara L: Can we add a required "verifier" field in the tracker? Right now items are marked done by owner and vanish. We need an independent check.

Nidhi (oncall): Also request: automated reminders at 48h and 7d before due_date. Oncall sees the downstream pain when items are stale.

Maria K: Good points. I'll add a verifier column and wire reminders via incidents-bot. Also adding a 90d stale flag that alerts eng leads (not auto-close).

Jamal R: If IC rotation owns facilitation, we need a checklist for them so it's low-friction. Alex, can you draft that?

Alex T: Yep. I'll draft a one-pager checklist and a short agenda template: 1) quick roll call, 2) review up to 8 open items (owner/ETA/blocker), 3) capture any items lacking owners, 4) tag follow-ups. Will attach sample query for monthly trends.

Sara L: Idea: classify remediation as code/process/infrastructure in tracker so we can heatmap the categories monthly.

Nidhi (oncall): For the reminders flow: can the bot create a short DM thread to owners instead of only channel pings? Less noise.

Maria K: Yes. Bot can DM owners and post a summary in #eng-oncall. We'll require at least one verifier and a due_date for every PM action before closing the PM.

Jamal R: What about escalation? If an item is flagged stale at 90d, should it escalate to the eng manager or the product lead?

Sara L: Escalate to the eng lead of the owning team and the incident PM. That keeps product informed of persistent gaps.

Alex T: For recurring patterns: monthly trends should include top 5 incident types, top 3 recurring remediations, and a small chart of incidents/week. I'll prototype a script to emit CSV/json.

Nidhi (oncall): Quick ops ask: can the weekly facilitator mark items as "blocked-by-oncall" to flag ops-level blockers? Helps us prioritize.

Maria K: Good call. Add a "blocking_context" tag to items. Also, weekly facilitator should update the tracker during the meeting. Keeps things current.

Jamal R: Volunteers for IC facilitation rotation: Jamal, Nidhi, Alex, Sara, Maria. I'll make a signup calendar.

Sara L: Micro-format for weekly notes: `item_id — owner (ETA) — 1-line blocker — verifier` That keeps entries consistent and quick to scan.

Alex T: I'll push a prototype query to the shared reports: https://go/reports/pm-remediations-proto (will be in the monthly deck).

Maria K: Action items from this thread: 
1) Alex: checklist + prototype metrics query (due Thu EOD).
2) Maria: add verifier + blocking_context columns to tracker + 48h/7d DM reminders via incidents-bot (due Fri).
3) Nidhi: test bot reminder flow on staging and report back here (due Tue).
4) Jamal: publish IC facilitation rotation calendar (due Mon).

Nidhi (oncall): I'll test the DM flow tomorrow and post logs here.

incidents-bot: Reminder scheduled: weekly "PM follow-ups" Mon 09:15-09:30. New tracker columns created: verifier, blocking_context, due_date_reminder.

Maria K: Plan looks good. If no objections I'll schedule the recurring 15m and upload the checklist + template to the tracker.

Jamal R: No objections. Thanks all.

Sara L: :+1: Schedule please.

Alex T: Will upload checklist and sample query link once done.

Maria K: Closing thread for now; will follow up with invites and links.
